display.purpose: Phase title at the head of the player aid (28px on phones); modal titles 26px.

headline.purpose: Player-aid section heads after the red rulebook number; top-bar phase label.

notation.purpose: Order notation such as A TEX - MEX; drafts 17px.

label.purpose: Uppercase condensed keys, track labels, buttons (15px), result words.

sea-name.purpose: Italic, 0.2em spaced sea names in sea-ink on the map; size set per zone.

shadows.value: solid offset fill, 1.3 units down-right (SVG); 2px right/bottom border on HTML counters
shadows.purpose: Die-cut thickness on counters, control markers, the turn counter and the Crisis marker only.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: Dialogs and the box lid, over a rgba(29, 29, 27, 0.5) backdrop.

motion.purpose: All placement motion: counter lift, turn counter, modal, bottom sheet.

motion.name: counter-lift
motion.purpose: Selected counter lifts 1.2 units up-left off its edge.

motion.name: counter-set
motion.purpose: Turn counter drops onto the current half from translate(-3px,-7px) rotate(-6deg).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion removes all animation and transition.

narrative.overview:
Brink is the 1970s Avalon Hill / SPI boxed wargame it descends from, printed and played on screen. The board is an offset-printed map sheet: flat blue-grey sea, buff and cream land stock, power homes as flat printed tints, black coastlines and dark-brown borders, italic letter-spaced sea names, condensed-caps lettering. Units are square die-cut counters in each power's printed stock, carrying a black NATO-style symbol and the power code, with a sliver of counter thickness showing at the bottom-right. Everything around the map is a player-aid card: black rules, numbered printed tracks, rulebook section numbers.

The density is a wargame's: a lot of state at once, held together by rules and type rather than by cards and whitespace. There is one theme, the light printed sheet (`color-scheme: light`; no dark mode). Corners are square everywhere. Depth is physical only where a physical object exists (a counter on the sheet); everything else is flat ink on paper.

The world explicitly rejects the flat SaaS dashboard that online Diplomacy boards default to: white cards, pill chips, Inter, big-number tiles.
keyCharacteristics: Printed map sheet with a double-rule neatline and a title cartouche; real Natural Earth geometry, never redrawn.
Die-cut counters (14-unit square, 1.3-unit edge) used identically on the map, in the player aid, the key and the start screen.
Every counter and control marker prints its power code; ownership never relies on colour alone.
Turn record track across the top: the game's clock and the replay scrubber.
Player-aid column of numbered sections keyed to the rulebook.
Two families only: Archivo (UI, body, logotype) and Barlow Condensed (all lettering, labels, numbers, notation).
Red is a spot colour with a job, never decoration.

rules.name: The Spot Red Rule
rules.body: Red marks the player's own action and Crisis danger. Beyond that it appears only as printed spot colour on the logotype box and rulebook section numbers. Other powers, failures and errors never get red.

rules.name: The Code-on-Every-Counter Rule
rules.body: No power is ever shown by colour alone. Counters, control markers and swatches all print the three-letter power code.

rules.name: The Derived Tint Rule
rules.body: Homes, swing states, edges and arrows are computed from the seven stocks by `mix()`. Add a power by adding one stock, never a hand-picked tint.

rules.name: The Two-Family Rule
rules.body: Archivo and Barlow Condensed only. Numbers that count (supply centres, scores, tally, Crisis) set in condensed 700 with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Spaced Sea Rule
rules.body: Sea names are italic and widely spaced (0.2em); land names are upright. The difference reads sea from land without colour.

rules.name: The Thickness-Is-Physical Rule
rules.body: A solid offset edge appears only on things that are counters: units, control markers, the game-turn counter, the Crisis marker. Don't use an offset edge to make a button or card look raised (the Commit button's 4px bottom lip, which presses to 2px, is the only pressable exception).

dos: Do draw every unit, swatch and marker with the shared counter drawing in `src/counter.ts`, printing the power code.
Do derive every power tint from the seven stocks in `src/theme.ts`.
Do head every player-aid section with its rulebook section number in red and condensed caps.
Do set lettering, labels, buttons, tracks and order notation in Barlow Condensed caps, with tabular figures for counts.
Do separate with ink rules (3 / 2 / 1.5 / 1px dotted) and keep corners square.
Do keep the map's projected geometry exactly as supplied in `board.json`, printed to the neatline.
Do keep the light printed sheet as the only theme.
donts: Don't use white cards, pill chips, Inter or big-number tiles; this is the SaaS dashboard the world refuses.
Don't use red for another power, a failed order, or general emphasis.
Don't show ownership by colour alone.
Don't give a non-counter element a die-cut edge to fake depth.
Don't use Unicode glyphs as icons; draw them as SVG at the controls' stroke weight.
